top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori, Ye) rests on one original idea, state-independent magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms. Its 10^-18 uncertainty is measured and checked in independent comparisons across several laboratories, and it is already used in relativistic geodesy and tests of constants. A citation worded around the lattice and many-atom interrogation separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, and the two-name allocation is the cleanest available. The unverified Sr/Yb first-demonstration history is a real residual weakness, but it does not justify withholding the prize.
